findings.evidence: `scripts/pr_status/labels.py:72-73,88-91` shows pending review alternates between `review-in-progress` and `awaiting-review` solely based on the live marker, while `review_cycle_metrics` at lines 321–324 counts every reapplication. The generated JSON’s 1,766 transitions since the 2026-07-22 label epoch is consistent with this inflation.
findings.fix: Reconstruct state intervals using both labeled and unlabeled events, and count/reset only transitions from an author-action/new-commit state into a genuinely new review cycle.
findings.issue: Counting every `awaiting-review` application as a new review cycle overcounts a single cycle whenever `review-in-progress` replaces that label and reconciliation later restores it; the same restoration also resets the current in-review clock at lines 301–304.

findings.evidence: Lines 243–259 filter only by marker and parse every `issue_url` suffix as a PR number; `scripts/housekeeping.py:27-30,120-126` confirms canonical scoreboards require a repo-associated author and shared metadata validation.
findings.fix: Restrict comments to numbers present in the fetched PR set and apply the repository’s canonical scoreboard trust/metadata validation before attribution.
findings.issue: `fetch_scoreboards` counts any repository issue comment containing the public marker, including comments on non-PR issues and marker comments from untrusted external users, so the chart is not a count of canonical PR review scoreboards.

summary: The review-cycle and contributor-review charts do not faithfully measure review cycles or canonical PR scoreboards.
